answer: Randomness-gated admission slots. Each epoch, a verifiable beacon (e.g., drand) produces a seed no one can precompute, seeding a lottery that assigns a limited pool of new identity slots; identities not selected that epoch must wait, and a glacier of accumulated pending registrations slows every later arrival. An attacker cannot target slots in advance, so each cohort needs a fresh ripple of real work plus a costly beacon-wait, and a fable of cheap mass registration collapses under the enforced per-identity delay and compute outlay.
